what: A rebuild of the v0.6.0 tag on a different machine from the one that published it, compared with the published archive
how: A fresh clone of the tag, built with build/make_gui.ps1 and build/make_release.py, then compared with the archive downloaded from the release page: the whole ZIP by SHA-256, and each executable by the digest the release run printed for it.

published_by.python: not captured from the run log; the workflow asks setup-python for 3.13

rebuilt_on.where: a personal Windows machine, from a fresh clone of the tag

what_this_does_not_show: Both machines ran the same in-box C# compiler build. A different compiler build has not been compared, so this does not establish that any Windows machine reproduces these bytes - only that these two did, and that the compiler is the variable the comparison did not vary.
The two machines did differ in operating-system build (Windows Server 2025 10.0.26100 against Windows 11 10.0.26200), so the result is not an artefact of one identical environment.

The runner's Python patch version was not captured. The archive is written by Python's zipfile and zlib, and the archives are byte-identical, so whatever it was it wrote the same bytes - but that is an observation, not a version that was read.
This is one measurement of one tag. Nothing here says the next release will reproduce.
